seal.statement: The owner's direction (2026-09-18) is that the hosted canary is for releases, an ordinary push should prove itself locally and in parallel across the lab machines, and no host belongs in any setup because the machines change: discover and measure what exists, then choose where to run what at test time. The lab tooling knew only each machine's OS and architecture. `lab fleet` now probes the controller and every inventory machine in parallel with ONE POSIX script - piped to sh locally, sent over ssh to a node, so the controller is never a special case - and records per machine: a boot identity, cores, memory, node version, whether a checkout of this repository exists and whether its lockfile and installed dependencies match the controller's, the digest-pinned MovieLens dataset the canary checks, docker, helm, wasm-tools, psql and a C++ compiler, and a fixed single-thread speed sample. Facts go into the out-of-repo inventory; readiness separates what disqualifies a machine from the corpus (node below the engines floor, no repository, a different lockfile, no dependencies) from gaps that placement can route around (tools and the dataset only some files need). First real run: controller 20 cores at speed x1.00 and ready; one lab node 12 cores x1.37 ready with gaps for the dataset, helm, wasm-tools and psql - exactly the five files that red there for setup reasons on 2026-09-17 - and another 8 cores x2.21 ready. Identity is the kernel's per-boot id, not /etc/machine-id: two machines in this lab share a machine-id because one was installed from the other's image, and the first version of this probe reported them as one machine. Nothing here decides placement; test-placement consumes these records.

text: scripts/lab/probe.js gains one capability script (sent to sh locally or over ssh), parseCapability, corpusReadiness and discoverFleet; scripts/lab/lagrange-lab.js gains lab fleet [--json], which records each machine's facts in the out-of-repo inventory and prints readiness with a speed factor relative to the controller. Two defects were found by running it against the real lab before any test existed: a linked worktree's .git is a file (so -e, not -d), and two lab machines share an /etc/machine-id because one was installed from the other's image (so identity is the per-boot id)

Round 1 reject. Blocking: cognitive complexity ratchet 161 over 160 after the fleet command grew; no test asserted ready === false for a null capability, an unreachable node or any single disqualifier; boot_id identity was unwitnessed. Non-blocking: nvm.sh sourced with the caller's positional parameters (a repo path of --install would run nvm install); dash echo rewrote backslashes; ssh unbounded (130 s against a blackholed address) and a target starting with - read as an option; docker info unbounded; version parse accepted v23-garbage; a missing lockfile requirement matched a machine with no lockfile; an unreachable machine's stale facts were indistinguishable from live ones; the node used and the probed path were not recorded; the node major was not passed.

Round-1 repairs. Script: set -- before sourcing nvm, printf-based say, repo_path, node_path, the engines-floor major passed and activated, timeout-bounded docker info, and installed-versus-lockfile compared by content (every required package at its locked version; optional ones may be absent) - the timestamp proxy first tried here reported the controller's linked worktree as stale. Lockfile digests read from stdin: GNU sha256sum prefixes the digest line with a backslash for a name holding one, which the new backslash-path test caught. parseCapability is three-valued through one flag reader. ssh gets ConnectTimeout and ServerAlive bounds and refuses a target starting with -. Versions must be exactly MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH; a requirement that is not a sha256 digest is never a match. recordFleet keeps an unreachable machine's last facts beside lastProbeFailure and clears it on an answer; formatFleet and the verdict helpers moved into probe.js so the command stays under the cognitive ratchet (160/160, cyclomatic 1819/1819). Tests: ready false for every disqualifier alone, null capability and the unreachable node; boot id equals the kernel's; a stub nvm records zero arguments, also for a --install path; backslash path and its lockfile digest; three dependency-match cases plus unknown; bounded ssh and the refused target; recordFleet and formatFleet. 13 mutations of the repairs all red.

Round 2 reject on one mechanical item: npm run audit:shards exited 1 because test/shards/subsystem-classes.json still recorded the fleet test as observing only the canary workflow, while the round-2 test also reads package-lock.json and env PATH (observationDigest b58a21c6 -> 503025b9); a stale entry also narrows impact selection. Every round-1 item re-checked and held: 26 mutations, 24 red; truncated transcripts never read ready; hostile paths under bash and dash ran nothing; a blackholed address bounded at 5.0 s; refused and option-shaped targets recorded as lastProbeFailure. Non-blocking: node -e read an option-shaped repo path as an option (a directory named --eval=... ran code); hard-coding nvm use 22 and dropping the docker bound stayed green; no overall per-probe deadline; unknown and different dependencies shared one reason; an unparsable engines floor read as node-too-old.

Round-2 repairs. subsystem-classes.json regenerated (audit:shards green). The dependency check runs node -e '...' -- "$repo", so an option-shaped path is only a path. The probe capture has a 60 s deadline (capture gains timeoutMs and SIGKILLs the child), on top of the ssh bounds. Readiness names dependencies-unknown apart from dependencies-differ-from-lockfile and no-node-floor apart from node-too-old; the requirement and repository checks moved into two helpers (cognitive 160/160, cyclomatic 1819/1819); version parsing is one parseVersion. Tests: the stub nvm records its call and must see `use 99` for a major no machine has; a stub timeout records `10 docker info` and docker then reads unreachable; a relative checkout path `--eval=...writeFileSync(...)` with a .git runs nothing; a hung child is killed at the deadline, not left running; four unparsable floors each give only no-node-floor. 7 mutations of these repairs all red.

Round 3 approve. audit:shards exits 0; cognitive 160/160, cyclomatic 1819/1819, unused exports 1438/1438; eslint, literals and fifteen cheap audits clean; harness 5/5, probe done. 20 mutations all red, including both round-2 survivors (hard-coded nvm use 22, unbounded docker info) and the round-3 repairs (no -- before the path, no deadline, capture rejecting without killing or ignoring timeoutMs). The --eval= directory that ran code in round 2 runs nothing; 18 hostile-path runs under simulated bash and dash remote parses created no canary. Real run 1.1 s: controller ready (dataset gap), one node ready with dataset, helm, wasm-tools and psql gaps, the inventory's own entry for the controller merged, another node ready with dataset, helm and wasm-tools gaps; absolute node paths recorded, dependencies current everywhere; a blackholed address bounded at 5.0 s. Non-blocking, carried to test-placement: the deadline SIGKILLs only the direct child, so a hung grandchild of the local sh -s survives and holds the pipe (the witness checks the dash pid, overstating what it proves) - fix with a process group and a grandchild witness; dependencies_current trusts npm's install record.
